passages.paragraph_text: So, there's a psychology around Kickstarter. At least this is the conventional thinking is that if you set your goal like really high, like if we would have set it to a million dollars, we probably wouldn't have made it. Because people would have looked at that and said like, oh, they'll never make it to a million dollars. And if you set it to 100,000, you know, us folks in the industry that are savvy about manufacturing will be like, oh, that's bullshit. They could never make all the tools. And so, what we did is we spent all summer beating up on the bill of materials. We reached out to a bunch of contract manufacturers. We want – these are the parts we want. And we worked on the bill of materials continually. And so, that's how we set the price. And then we extrapolated out off of our units that we needed to sell. And that's how we came up with our total unit price. And 400K was what Rick and I, we sat down and were like, okay, if we only get 400K, can we do it if we threw our own money in there just in case something horrible went wrong? Yep. And that's what we did. It's like 400K, maybe we'd have to chip in another 100K if something bad went wrong. So, and that's how we came up with the number. And I don't – I'm not sure if it hurt us or not because as soon as we hit 400K, like, our pledges went way down. So –
